project_description: A web-based application designed to digitalize and streamline the employee leave application, approval, and management process, replacing current manual tracking methods.

executive_summary.project_overview: The Employee Leave Management System is a comprehensive web-based platform aimed at digitizing the entire leave lifecycle. It will provide capabilities for employees to apply for leave, for managers to efficiently review and action those requests, and for HR administrators to manage leave policies and employee accounts.
executive_summary.business_problem: The current manual leave tracking process is inefficient, prone to errors, and generates significant paperwork. This leads to delays in leave approvals, difficulties in maintaining accurate leave balances, and challenges in generating comprehensive leave reports, impacting operational efficiency and employee satisfaction.
executive_summary.business_need: There is a critical business need for a centralized, digital solution to simplify the leave application process, ensure accurate maintenance of leave balances, empower managers with streamlined approval workflows, and provide an accessible record of leave history for all stakeholders. This will significantly reduce manual paperwork and administrative overhead.
executive_summary.proposed_solution: The proposed solution is a web-based Employee Leave Management System comprising distinct modules for Employees, Managers, and HR Administrators. It will offer secure login, real-time leave balance display, an intuitive leave application interface, a dashboard for managers to approve/reject requests with comments, and administrative tools for HR to manage policies, accounts, and generate reports.
business_benefits: Streamlined leave application and approval processes.
Enhanced accuracy and real-time visibility of leave balances.
Reduced administrative burden and paperwork for HR and employees.
Improved operational efficiency through digital workflows.
Increased employee satisfaction due to simplified self-service options.
Better compliance and reporting capabilities for HR.
executive_summary.expected_outcome: The successful implementation of the Employee Leave Management System will result in a fully digitalized, efficient, and transparent leave management process across the organization. It is anticipated to significantly reduce manual intervention, improve data accuracy, provide better insights into leave trends, and foster a more productive work environment.

epics.title: Employee Self-Service Leave Management
epics.business_objective: To empower employees with a secure and intuitive platform for managing their personal leave requests and viewing their leave information digitally.
epics.business_value: Enables employees to independently apply for, track, and manage their leave, reducing reliance on manual HR intervention and increasing transparency. This leads to higher employee satisfaction and reduced administrative queries.
epics.detailed_description: This epic focuses on developing all functionalities necessary for employees to interact with the leave management system. It includes secure authentication, the ability to view personal leave balances, apply for various leave types, specify leave dates and reasons, cancel pending requests, and access their comprehensive leave history.
scope: Display of individual leave balances by type.
Selection of different leave types (e.g., annual, sick).
Input of start and end dates for leave requests.
Provision of a mandatory reason for leave.
Ability to view the status of pending leave requests.
Cancellation of self-submitted pending leave requests.
Access to a historical record of all past leave applications and their outcomes.
out_of_scope: Integration with payroll systems for salary deductions related to unpaid leave.
Complex leave accrual rule configuration by employees.
Direct communication features between employee and HR/manager within the system (beyond comments).
assumptions: Employees have stable internet access to use the web application.
Each employee belongs to exactly one department.
Each employee has a single designated reporting manager.
Leave balances are reset annually according to company policy.
Employees will be provided with login credentials by HR.
dependencies: Availability of a secure authentication service.
Backend services to manage leave balances and request states.
Manager Module for processing submitted leave requests.
risks: Low user adoption if the interface is not intuitive.
Data accuracy issues if integration with existing HRIS is complex.
Security vulnerabilities if authentication mechanisms are not robust.
success_metrics: Percentage of leave requests submitted digitally (target: 95%).
Reduction in employee queries related to leave balances (target: 30%).
Average time taken for an employee to submit a leave request (target: < 2 minutes).
User satisfaction score for the employee module (target: 4/5).

features.title: Employee Leave Application Workflow
features.description: Enables employees to securely log in, view their current leave balances, and submit new leave requests, including selecting leave types, specifying dates, and providing reasons.
functional_requirements: Employees shall be able to login securely.
Employees shall be able to view available leave balance.
Employees shall be able to apply for leave.
Employees shall be able to select leave type.
Employees shall be able to enter leave dates.
Employees shall be able to provide leave reason.
non_functional_requirements: Response time below 2 seconds for all user interactions.
Responsive web interface compatible with major browsers and devices.
technical_notes: Authentication service will likely leverage OAuth2/JWT tokens.
Frontend will use a modern JavaScript framework (e.g., React, Angular, Vue).
API endpoints for balance retrieval and leave submission will be RESTful.
dependencies: Backend database for storing leave requests and user data.
acceptance_criteria: A registered employee can log in successfully with valid credentials.
The employee's current leave balances for all applicable types are displayed accurately upon login.
An employee can successfully submit a leave request, providing all mandatory details (type, dates, reason).
The system prevents submission of leave requests for dates in the past.
The system validates leave dates to ensure they are continuous (for single period requests) or within policy limits.
A confirmation message is displayed upon successful submission of a leave request.

features.title: Employee Leave History and Request Management
features.description: Provides employees with the ability to view their submitted leave requests, including pending ones, and to cancel requests that have not yet been approved by their manager.
functional_requirements: Employees shall be able to cancel pending leave requests.
Employees shall be able to view leave history.
non_functional_requirements: Response time below 2 seconds for all data retrieval operations.
Data privacy must be maintained for all personal leave history.
The system must maintain high availability for employees to access their information.
technical_notes: Leave history will be paginated and sortable by date or status.
Cancellation will trigger an update in the backend and potentially a notification to the manager.
Frontend component to display tabular data for requests.
dependencies: Notification Service (for manager alerts on cancellation).
acceptance_criteria: An employee can view a list of all their leave requests, showing status (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled).
An employee can filter or sort their leave history by status or date range.
An employee can select a 'Pending' leave request and successfully initiate its cancellation.
Upon successful cancellation, the request status is updated to 'Cancelled' and removed from the manager's pending queue.
The system prevents cancellation of leave requests that are already Approved or Rejected.

epics.title: Manager and HR Administrative Leave Operations
epics.business_objective: To provide managers with efficient tools for reviewing and actioning employee leave requests and to equip HR administrators with comprehensive capabilities for policy, account, and reporting management.
epics.business_value: Improves organizational efficiency by streamlining critical approval workflows and centralizing all HR-related leave administration. Ensures compliance with company policies and provides valuable insights through reporting, reducing operational risks and manual overhead.
epics.detailed_description: This epic encompasses the functionalities for managers to effectively approve or reject employee leave requests, including the ability to add comments for rejections. It also covers the HR module, allowing administrators to create and manage employee accounts, modify organizational leave policies, update individual leave balances, and generate organization-wide leave reports.
scope: Managers viewing a dashboard of pending leave requests from their direct reports.
Mandatory comment entry for managers when rejecting a leave request.
Managers viewing the leave history for their direct reports.
HR administrators creating new employee accounts within the system.
HR administrators modifying system-wide leave policies (e.g., accrual rules, maximum carry-over).
HR administrators manually updating individual employee leave balances.
HR administrators generating and viewing organization-wide leave reports (e.g., leave taken by department, upcoming leave).
out_of_scope: Automated leave accrual calculations based on complex rules (initial focus is on HR updating balances).
Integration with Active Directory or LDAP for user provisioning (initial focus is on HR creating accounts).
Advanced analytics dashboards beyond basic reporting.
assumptions: Managers will receive training on using the approval workflow.
HR administrators have the necessary authority and knowledge to configure policies and manage accounts.
Access to HR functionalities will be strictly controlled via role-based access.
Compliance with data privacy regulations will be maintained for all sensitive employee data.
dependencies: Employee Module for generating leave requests.
Secure User Authentication and Authorization services.
Robust database for storing all configuration, policy, and transactional data.
risks: Incorrect policy configuration by HR leading to system errors.
Security breaches if role-based access control is not properly implemented.
Performance degradation if reporting queries are not optimized.
Manager resistance to using a new digital system over existing manual processes.
success_metrics: Average time for managers to approve/reject requests (target: < 24 hours).
Number of manual leave balance adjustments by HR (target: minimized post-initial setup).
Security audit findings (target: zero critical vulnerabilities).

features.title: Manager Leave Request Approval Workflow
features.description: Provides managers with a dedicated interface to view, approve, or reject pending leave requests from their direct reports, including the ability to provide comments for rejections.
functional_requirements: Managers shall be able to view pending leave requests.
Managers shall be able to approve requests.
Managers shall be able to reject requests.
Managers shall be able to add comments while rejecting.
Managers shall be able to view employee leave history.
non_functional_requirements: Role-based access control to ensure managers only see their direct reports' requests.
Response time below 2 seconds for loading pending requests and actioning them.
High availability to ensure managers can action requests promptly.
Secure audit trail for all manager actions (approvals/rejections).
technical_notes: Manager dashboard will display a list of pending requests with key details (employee, type, dates).
API endpoints for approving, rejecting, and retrieving employee leave history.
Notifications (e.g., email) to employees upon manager action.
acceptance_criteria: A manager can successfully log in and view a dashboard showing all pending leave requests from their direct reports.
For each pending request, the manager can see employee name, leave type, dates, and reason.
A manager can select a request and approve it, updating the status and notifying the employee.
A manager can select a request and reject it, providing a mandatory comment, updating the status, and notifying the employee.
Managers can access the full leave history for any of their direct reports.

features.title: HR Administration and Reporting
features.description: Empowers HR administrators with tools to manage employee accounts, define and update leave policies, adjust leave balances, and generate comprehensive organization-wide leave reports.
functional_requirements: HR administrators shall be able to create employee accounts.
HR administrators shall be able to modify leave policies.
HR administrators shall be able to update leave balances.
HR administrators shall be able to view organization-wide leave reports.
non_functional_requirements: Role-based access control to restrict HR functionalities to authorized users.
Data integrity and validation for policy modifications and balance updates.
Daily database backup schedule to prevent data loss.
Scalability to handle increased employee count and reporting data volume.
Reliability of reporting engine for accurate and timely data generation.
technical_notes: Dedicated HR administration portal with appropriate security measures.
Backend services for user provisioning, policy management, and balance updates.
Reporting module to aggregate and visualize leave data, possibly using a separate reporting database or data warehouse if complexity requires.
acceptance_criteria: An HR administrator can create a new employee account, including initial leave balances, and assign a manager.
An HR administrator can modify global leave policies (e.g., annual leave accrual, sick leave limits) and save these changes.
An HR administrator can search for an employee and manually adjust their leave balance for a specific leave type.
An HR administrator can generate an organization-wide report showing leave taken by department for a specified period.
The system ensures an audit trail for all HR-initiated changes to policies and employee balances.

non_functional_requirements.performance: All core system functionalities, including page loads, data retrieval (e.g., leave history, pending requests), and transaction processing (e.g., leave submission, approval), shall have a response time of less than 2 seconds under normal load conditions (up to 50 concurrent users). Reporting functions may have longer acceptable response times, up to 10 seconds for complex, organization-wide reports.
non_functional_requirements.security: The system shall implement secure authentication mechanisms (e.g., multi-factor authentication, strong password policies) and role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure users can only access authorized functionalities and data (e.g., employees only their data, managers only their direct reports, HR only administrative functions). All data in transit and at rest shall be encrypted using industry-standard protocols. The system shall be protected against common web vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10) through secure coding practices and regular security audits. Daily database backup procedures must be implemented for disaster recovery.
non_functional_requirements.availability: The system shall be available 99.5% of the time during business hours (9 AM - 5 PM, Monday-Friday), excluding planned maintenance windows. Critical functionalities like employee login and leave application should aim for 99.9% availability. Regular backups and a robust disaster recovery plan shall be in place to minimize downtime in case of critical failures.
non_functional_requirements.scalability: The system shall be designed to scale horizontally to support up to 5,000 employees and 500 concurrent users without significant degradation in performance. This includes scaling for increased data storage, transaction volume, and reporting demands. The architecture should support adding more resources (servers, database capacity) as the organization grows.
non_functional_requirements.reliability: The system shall maintain data integrity across all operations, ensuring that leave balances, request statuses, and policy configurations are consistently accurate. Automated error logging and monitoring shall be in place to detect and alert on system failures. Transactional operations (e.g., leave submission, approval) must be atomic and fault-tolerant, ensuring that either the entire operation succeeds or fails gracefully without corrupting data. Daily database backups are a critical component of data reliability.
